definitions.explanation: A plant of the Brassica family grown for its oil-rich seeds and as a green vegetable. Its bright yellow flowers are an iconic sight of spring in Japan.

examples.japanese: {油菜|あぶらな}の{花|はな}が{咲|さ}いている。
{春|はる}になると、{畑|はたけ}が{油菜|あぶらな}の{黄色|きいろ}で{染|そ}まる。
examples.english: When spring comes, the fields are dyed yellow with rapeseed.

examples.japanese: {油菜|あぶらな}は{食用|しょくよう}としても{栽培|さいばい}され、おひたしや{炒|いた}め{物|もの}にして{食|た}べる。
examples.english: Rapeseed is also grown as a food crop and eaten as boiled greens or in stir-fries.

notes:
Literally 'oil vegetable' — named because its seeds are pressed to produce cooking oil ({菜種油|なたねあぶら}). The plant is also known as {菜|な}の{花|はな} (canola flower), especially when referring to the flowers or the plant as a spring symbol.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Fields of brilliant yellow {油菜|あぶらな} flowers are a beloved spring sight in Japan. {菜|な}の{花|はな} is a seasonal word ({季語|きご}) for spring in haiku. The plant is also eaten as a vegetable — the young shoots and flower buds are a spring delicacy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {油菜|あぶらな}の{花|はな} — rapeseed flower
- {菜種|なたね}{油|あぶら} — rapeseed oil, canola oil
- {油菜|あぶらな}{畑|ばたけ} — rapeseed field

RELATED WORDS:
- {菜|な}の{花|はな} — canola flower; the popular name for the flowers and the edible shoots
- {菜種|なたね} — rapeseed; refers specifically to the seeds
- {白菜|はくさい} — Chinese cabbage; a related Brassica vegetable
